findings.trigger: On macOS/POSIX, an unapproved symlink in ios/Pods or node_modules has a name without a native suffix and points to a directory containing native payload.
findings.evidence: inventory uses os.walk(..., followlinks=False), but its directory and file branches do not reject a POSIX symlink unless its path is classified native. For a non-native linked entry, line 142 skips magic-byte probing and line 146 does not record it; a directory symlink is not descended. A synthetic production-inventory probe modeling the POSIX directory-entry shape returned an empty manifest while the target contained hidden-native.a. This was not a real POSIX filesystem test: creating a POSIX symlink on this Windows host failed with WinError 1314.
findings.disposition: Block candidate bootstrap. Per the caller's final-review constraint, do not start another same-class repair/review or CI run in this round; preserve this as an unresolved blocker.

findings.trigger: An unapproved POSIX link without a native-suffix path component hides native dependency bytes from the inventory.
findings.evidence: The non-native linked-entry branches neither reject the link nor traverse it; the mocked production-path probe produced an empty schema-v2 manifest despite a synthetic native file at the target. The test suite covers the six exact Hermes aliases, known Hermes prefixes, and Windows junction negatives, but does not cover this unapproved no-suffix POSIX-link case. No real POSIX execution is claimed.
findings.disposition: Same blocker as the security report; bootstrap remains unsafe and no fix or further same-class attempt was made.
